provider: GitLab Package Registry (generic / npm / Maven / PyPI / NuGet / Conan)

free_tier.stated: Explicitly EXCLUDED from the project storage quota. GitLab docs, verbatim: 'GitLab projects have a storage limit for their Git repository and Large File Storage (LFS). Only the project's repository and LFS are included in the storage limit. The container registry, package registry, and build artifacts are not included in the limit.' The 10 GiB figure (pricing page: 'Storage 10 GiB') therefore applies only to git+LFS; package bytes are unquota'd. Per-file ceilings: Generic 5 GB, npm 5 GB, Maven 5 GB, NuGet 5 GB, PyPI 5 GB, Conan 5 GB, Terraform 1 GB, ML model 10 GB (uploads capped at 5 GB), Helm 5 MB.

egress.terms: Free and unmetered for downloads; no egress line item anywhere in GitLab pricing. Served through Cloudflare (probe returned Server: cloudflare).

tooling: Full REST API: PUT /api/v4/projects/:id/packages/generic/:package_name/:version/:file_name and GET the same path for download. Also native npm/maven/pypi/nuget/conan clients by pointing a user at the GitLab URL. No rclone backend, but the generic-package PUT/GET is a two-verb blob API — trivial to drive from curl or a 30-line Python loop. Deploy tokens with write_package_registry scope give scoped push credentials.
chaining: UNBOUNDED on two axes: (a) unlimited free projects per account (GitLab Free has no project cap; only project creation rate is limited to 200/day/user) x 5 GB per file x unlimited files per project; (b) package bytes sit outside the 10 GiB quota entirely, so a single project is already a de-facto unlimited bucket and additional projects multiply it further.
limits_note: 5 GB per file (generic). Package registry rate limits apply to the Packages API. Authenticated API traffic 2,000 req/min per user; unauthenticated 60 req/hr per IP. Project creation 200/day/user. No per-project package storage cap documented.
reliability_note: Package registry is a real feature not a cache — no TTL, but a project cleanup policy can auto-delete package assets if configured, so leave it off. Anonymous pull must be enabled per project ('Allow anyone to pull from package registry'). NuGet group endpoints refuse anonymous pulls entirely.
